keys: `run: webhook` POSTs JSON to `with.url` (Content-Type application/json) and waits up to 10 s for the answer. The body is `payload:` (a map or list, each `${{ }}` value resolved like a respond `json:` value) or `body:` (text sent as written; a map or list there is the same as payload); both together are refused. With neither, the step posts the whole flow context, so always write one. It takes no method, headers, auth or `sign:` and has no outputs: use `run: api` to set those or to read the answer.
result: Only a 2xx answer is success: any other status, a timeout or a private or internal address fails the step, and five failures in a row pause calls to that host (circuit_breaker). A value in the URL or the body that does not resolve fails the step before anything is sent. Refused in a `transaction: true` flow (transactional_sends).
yaml_example:
# flows/task-webhook.yaml - POST one task to an outside URL as JSON
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/tasks/:id/announce
    auth: required
jobs:
  announce:
    steps:
      - id: task
        run: sql
        expect_rows: "=1"
        with: { query: "SELECT id, title, status FROM tasks WHERE id = :id AND user_id = :user_id" }
      - run: webhook
        with:
          url: "${{ env.TASK_WEBHOOK_URL }}"            # your endpoint, kept in env
          payload:                                      # the JSON body
            event: task.announced
            task: { id: "${{ steps.task.outputs.id }}", title: "${{ steps.task.outputs.title }}" }
            done: "${{ steps.task.outputs.status == 'done' }}"
      - run: respond
        with: { status: 200, json: { announced: true } }
